input: arr1 and arr2 have lengths n,m<=2000 and integer values in[0,1000000000]. Empty arrays are accepted extensions; replacements can reuse any arr2 value. Collections are ordinary finite dense arrays/lists, not subclasses, proxies, sparse/accessor-backed collections. Strings are ordinary/primitive strings. Every collection length and computed allocation size fits [0,4294967295], with padded sizes explicitly included. No concurrent mutation or built-in monkey-patching is allowed. Preconditions are not runtime-checked, and allocation/resource capacity or completion is not guaranteed by declared bounds. Python integer inputs are plain int, excluding bool.
return: Minimum replacements of arr1 positions with values from arr2 needed to make arr1 strictly increasing, or-1 if impossible.
mutation_aliasing: Sorts arr2 ascending in place, then compacts distinct values into its prefix without truncating its length; trailing cells retain the post-sort values not overwritten by that compaction. arr1 is unchanged. A private slice of the unique prefix supplies DP replacements.
numeric: The initial previous=-1 is below every permitted value. DP costs are in[0,n], with n+1 used as a finite absent-cost sentinel; nullish lookup preserves a stored zero cost. For a fixed predecessor, only the smallest larger replacement is needed because it dominates larger choices at equal cost. All integer inputs/intermediates remain within [-9007199254740991,9007199254740991]; no bitwise coercion is used.
complexity: Expected O(m log(m+1)+n*(m+1)*log(m+1)+n+1) time and O(m+1) live auxiliary space, including replacement storage, sort workspace, and a constant number of state maps of at most m+1 entries each. Hash/sort assumptions are explicit. Bounds include ordinary built-in operations/allocations and assume bounded-word arithmetic, constant-time indexing, amortized append/pop and any explicitly stated hash/sort behavior.

helpers.name: upper_bound
helpers.contract: First sorted replacement strictly larger than previous, without adding one to previous.
helpers.cost: O(log(m+1)) time/O(1) space per state, byte-identical to0034 helper. Its complete definition is 285 UTF-8 bytes; separator newlines count toward total source bytes.

source_accounting: The complete standalone source is 1277 UTF-8 bytes, including every helper, Solution wrapper, signature, loop, built-in call, annotation/comment, whitespace and terminal newline. Helpers are fully charged per candidate, not free shared libraries. No imports, runtime-generated implementations or hidden source expansion are used. Any eventual judge-interface adapter is additional charged source.

The new mutation/identity contract matches the frozen predecessor observation contract; this does not itself establish fresh behavioral qualification, complexity qualification or M1. All source/helper/adapter costs remain charged.
